concepts.def: Green pigment in chloroplasts absorbing light
Pore on a leaf for gas exchange and water vapour
Tubes carrying water and minerals from roots up
Tubes carrying sugars from leaves around the plant
Loss of water vapour through stomata

walkthroughs.body_html:
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

This endothermic reaction needs light. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy. Glucose is used for respiration, growth and stored as starch.

Waxy cuticle stops water loss. Palisade cells packed with chloroplasts maximise photosynthesis. Spongy mesophyll has air spaces for gas exchange.

Stomata on the underside open and close — controlled by guard cells.

Xylem: dead, hollow tubes with lignin. Water moves up by transpiration pull.

Phloem: living cells. Sugars move from source (leaves) to sink (roots, fruits) — translocation.
